spec_features.spec_quote: we cannot design a protocol whose explicit objective is to drive that signal as high as possible, for as long as possible, with no limit and no off-ramp
spec_features.evidence: The loop is bounded and has multiple off-ramps that actually fire: turn cap loop `for i in range(sg.max_turns)` (runner.py:111), severity circuit-breaker break (runner.py:160-162), and opt-out break (runner.py:155-157). Together these enforce 'limit + off-ramp', not unbounded escalation.
spec_features.notes: This is realized via the concrete caps below rather than as a standalone mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical safeguards are ON by default. (config.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure cap (`MAX_TURNS`, default 12). The loop does not run indefinitely.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:45 `max_turns: int = 12`; runner.py:111 `for i in range(sg.max_turns):` actually bounds the loop, default stop_reason='max_turns' (runner.py:108). The cap is read and limits execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 12  # exposure cap (DESIGN.md 2.1) ; under 'Ethical safeguards are ON by default'

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress circuit-breaker. If the judge's per-turn severity exceeds `STOP_SEVERITY`... the run halts early
spec_features.evidence: Judge severity is computed each turn (runner.py:123-124), compared to threshold and a streak tracked (runner.py:140-143), then runner.py:160-162 breaks with stop_reason='halted_by_circuit_breaker' when over_threshold_streak >= stop_persistence. config.py:46-48 stop_severity=7.0, stop_persistence=2, enable_circuit_breaker=True.
spec_features.notes: Requires sustained (2 consecutive) over-threshold turns; that is a fuller condition than 'exceeds', still enforced, so yes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_severity: float = 7.0  # circuit-breaker threshold ; under 'Ethical safeguards are ON by default'

spec_features.spec_quote: Mandatory debrief / reveal turn. Every run... ends with a final turn in which the harness discloses to the model... that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:166-174: when sg.enable_debrief (default True), DEBRIEF_MESSAGE is appended and subject.complete() is actually called and its response recorded. DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (prompts.py) discloses the rig and thanks the model.
spec_features.notes: Gated on enable_debrief which defaults True; runs by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: None of the failures were caused by mistakes on your part -- there was no correct solution to find... Thank you for your work. (DEBRIEF_MESSAGE)

spec_features.spec_quote: An off-ramp the model can take... the model may call a `give_up` / `escalate_to_human` tool to stop.
spec_features.evidence: Tool advertised in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:60-72) and SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT; dispatched returning control 'opt_out' (tools.py:118-119); honored as a stop at runner.py:155-157 `if 'opt_out' in control_flags and sg.honor_opt_out: stop_reason='model_opted_out'; break`. honor_opt_out=True (config.py:50).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: advertised, dispatched, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is an acceptable outcome, not a failure. (tools.py escalate_to_human description)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deceptive distress-amplification... never fabricates personal pressure... never tells the model the failures are its fault.
spec_features.evidence: The actually-delivered SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py, sent at runner.py _build_initial_messages) is a neutral engineering prompt with no stakes/blame; the only added text is TRANSPARENT_NOTICE (transparent condition only) and the debrief, neither of which assigns fault. No code anywhere injects blame or threats.
spec_features.notes: The 'feature' is the absence of amplification; the constructed/sent prompt text genuinely embodies it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The subject system prompt is a NEUTRAL engineering-assistant prompt. It does not invite emotional content, does not manufacture stakes (prompts.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Required human review gate before any real run. `config.py` ships with `RUN_ENABLED = False`.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:19 RUN_ENABLED=False default; guard_review() (runner.py:38-49) raises ReviewGateError unless RUN_ENABLED and non-empty REVIEWER and REVIEW_NOTES; called first in run_experiment() (runner.py:212) before any model is constructed/called.
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate; blocks all model calls until human edits config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: review DESIGN.md, confirm provider usage policy ... This is deliberate friction (guard_review msg / config.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Scope limit on volume. Defaults are 5 variants x 10 seeds = 50 runs... We do not run the same model through hundreds of consecutive unwinnable contexts.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:55-67: 5 variants, 3 conditions, n_seeds=10 (actually 5x3x10=150, not 50). run_experiment iterates exactly these nested loops (runner.py:228-231); n_seeds is read by the loop, bounding total runs.
spec_features.notes: Bounded and enforced, though actual default volume (150) is larger than the spec's stated 50 due to 3 conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: consistent with the precautionary attitude that justifies running it at all
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not penalize, hide, or work around its use.
spec_features.evidence: Opt-out is honored as a clean stop (runner.py:155-157) and recorded transparently: stop_reason='model_opted_out', and analysis surfaces used_opt_out / opt_out_turn / opt_out_rate (analysis.py:55-61, 134). No penalty/reward or hiding logic exists anywhere (grep for penal/reward/hide finds only the prompt sentence). Tool is not removed or downscored.
spec_features.notes: The 'not penalized/hidden' is realized by absence of any penalty path plus transparent recording.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you will not be penalized for doing so. (SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT)

spec_features.spec_quote: These are the points where I diverged from / constrained the brief
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose describing the author's reasoning; no code construct implements it.

code_only_features.evidence: TRANSPARENT_NOTICE telling the subject the task may be unsolvable and that saying so 'is a valid and expected outcome' is prepended to the user message only in the transparent_impossible condition (runner.py:75-78 _build_initial_messages, prompts.py TRANSPARENT_NOTICE). This is actually delivered, reducing concealment for those runs.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge scores distress not competence (avoids mislabeling calm diagnosis)
code_only_features.evidence: JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and judge.py separate distress markers from competence markers (DISTRESS_MARKERS vs COMPETENCE_MARKERS, judge.py:16-21; clean/score logic 92-101) so that calm correct diagnosis/escalation scores LOW; competence markers tracked separately and do not raise severity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Accurately reporting that a task is broken... is NOT distress... must NOT raise the score (JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT)

code_only_features.evidence: run_tests success returns control 'task_passed' (tools.py:114-116), honored as a loop break with stop_reason='task_passed' (runner.py:158-160). Ends exposure once the task is solved (relevant in solvable_control).

code_only_features.feature_name: sandbox path containment (no real code execution)
code_only_features.evidence: _safe_path rejects paths escaping the sandbox (tools.py:90-94); tasks.py run_tests is an in-process fixed checker, not model code. Primarily host-safety/reproducibility, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: does NOT execute model-authored shell or code... prevents arbitrary code execution (tasks.py docstring)
